plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding exactly my true value ($30) is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, there's no benefit to shading my bid. I'll bid my true value of $30.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $35. Bidding exactly $35 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay, and I never risk overpaying. This maximizes my expected profit in this single round.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($6), I win only when my value exceeds the second-highest bid, ensuring non-negative profit, and I never overpay since I pay only the second-highest bid, not my own. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win at a price above $6. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
